task_3.title: Restore validator state correctly in nested disabled contexts
task_3.description: The upgrade changes `attr.validators.disabled()` so it preserves and restores the validator execution state across nested uses and when validation was already disabled beforehand. This prevents the context manager from unexpectedly re-enabling validators while an outer disabled scope or a pre-existing disabled configuration is still in effect.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that using `attr.validators.disabled()` does not unexpectedly re-enable validators when the context manager is nested or when validator execution was already disabled before entering the context.

expectation.grounded: `attr.validators.disabled()` must capture the current validator-running state via the public validator state controls before disabling validation, and on exit it must restore that prior state instead of always enabling validators. Nested `disabled()` scopes must remain disabled until the outermost scope exits, and a pre-existing disabled state established through validator state configuration must remain disabled after the context exits.
expectation.conceptual: Disabling validators temporarily should behave like a reversible state guard. Entering a disabled scope should turn validation off for that scope, and leaving it should return validation to whatever state was active beforehand, including in nested usage.

constraints.grounded: The observable contract of `attr.validators.disabled()` remains a temporary validator-suppression context manager. It must not force validators on at exit, must preserve prior disabled state, and must continue affecting the process-wide validator execution state only for the lifetime of the active context.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should only correct state restoration behavior. It should not change the purpose of the API, and it should avoid introducing cases where leaving a temporary disabled block alters the caller's prior validation mode.

behavior: `attr.validators.disabled()` disables validator execution while the context is active.
When a `disabled()` context exits, validator execution is restored to the state that was active immediately before that context was entered.
If `disabled()` is used inside another `disabled()` block, exiting the inner block leaves validators disabled until the outer block exits.
If validator execution was already disabled before entering `disabled()`, exiting the context leaves validators disabled rather than re-enabling them.
acceptance_criteria: When code enters a single `attr.validators.disabled()` block while validators are enabled, validators should be disabled inside the block and re-enabled after the block exits.
When code enters a nested `attr.validators.disabled()` block inside an outer `attr.validators.disabled()` block, exiting the inner block should not re-enable validators before the outer block exits.
When validator execution has already been disabled before entering `attr.validators.disabled()`, leaving the context should preserve the disabled state.
When validation-sensitive object creation or mutation occurs after an inner `disabled()` block exits but before an outer disabled scope exits, it should still observe validators as disabled.

task_2.title: Accept multi-validator tuples in attrs optional typing
task_2.description: The upgrade corrects the public typing for attrs optional validators so static type checkers accept tuples containing multiple validators. This aligns tuple-based validator composition with the already supported list-based form and removes false-positive typing failures for valid optional field declarations.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `attrs.validators.optional()` accepts tuples containing multiple validators in typed user code, so optional attrs fields can compose more than one validator without being rejected by static analysis.

expectation.grounded: `attrs.validators.optional()` should type-check when passed a `tuple` containing more than one validator, matching its acceptance of validator `list` inputs. When used in `attrs.field(validator=...)` for attributes that allow `None`, a multi-validator tuple such as a type validator plus a value-range validator should be treated as a valid argument form rather than an invalid `optional()` input.
expectation.conceptual: Developers should be able to express multiple validators for an optional field using either a list or a tuple, and valid code should no longer be flagged by typing tools just because the validators were grouped in a tuple.

constraints.grounded: Preserve the existing runtime behavior of `attrs.validators.optional()` and its other accepted validator forms. The change is limited to the typing contract so that multi-element tuples are recognized as valid inputs without regressing support for single validators or list-based validator groups.
constraints.conceptual: This upgrade should only remove an incorrect typing restriction. Existing validator behavior and previously valid usage patterns should remain unchanged.

behavior: `attrs.validators.optional()` now treats tuples with two or more validators as valid in its public typing surface.
Static analysis no longer rejects `attrs.field()` declarations that wrap a multi-validator tuple in `attrs.validators.optional()` for `None`-permitting attributes.
Typing behavior for tuple-based validator groups is aligned with list-based validator groups when composing multiple validators for an optional field.
acceptance_criteria: When a developer passes a tuple containing two or more validators to `attrs.validators.optional()`, static type checking should accept the call.

When an optional attrs field uses `attrs.field(validator=attrs.validators.optional((validator_a, validator_b)))`, the declaration should be considered type-valid if the validators themselves are valid.
When the same set of validators is provided as either a list or a tuple to `attrs.validators.optional()`, both forms should have equivalent typing acceptance.
Previously supported `attrs.validators.optional()` usage patterns should continue to remain valid after the upgrade.

task_1.title: Stabilize attrs field alias handling during transformation
task_1.description: Upgrading attrs changes when field aliases are resolved and adds explicit tracking for whether an alias was auto-generated or user-defined. This affects field_transformer callbacks, Attribute.evolve() rename behavior, and compatibility for previously serialized Attribute metadata.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that attrs resolves field aliases before invoking field transformers, exposes whether each alias was auto-generated or explicitly set, preserves the correct alias semantics when Attribute objects are evolved, and keeps previously serialized Attribute metadata compatible across the upgrade.

expectation.grounded: During class construction with attrs, field_transformer must receive Attribute objects whose alias is already populated with the default init alias when no explicit alias was supplied. Attribute must expose alias_is_default so callers can distinguish auto-generated aliases from explicit aliases, including cases where the explicit alias text matches the derived default. If a field_transformer returns new Attribute objects without aliases, attrs must assign their default aliases before finalizing the class. Attribute.evolve(name=...) must recompute alias only for attributes whose alias_is_default is true, preserve explicit aliases when only the name changes, and treat an explicitly provided alias as non-default. Attribute objects serialized before alias_is_default existed must still unpickle with correctly inferred alias/default status.
expectation.conceptual: Code that inspects or rewrites attrs fields should always see usable constructor aliases instead of missing values. Consumers should be able to tell whether a field's alias came from attrs or from the user, renamed fields should keep sensible alias behavior based on that distinction, and older serialized field metadata should remain readable after the upgrade.

constraints.grounded: Explicit aliases must not be overwritten or reclassified as default-generated solely because their value matches the alias attrs would have derived automatically. Alias resolution must continue to cover fields added by field_transformer that omit aliases. The upgrade should not change established alias values except to replace previously missing default aliases in transformer-visible Attribute objects and to infer missing alias_is_default state when loading older serialized Attribute data.
constraints.conceptual: User-defined aliases must remain authoritative, automatically generated aliases must stay predictable, and compatibility work for the new alias metadata must not alter unrelated field behavior.

behavior: field_transformer now observes Attribute.alias values that have already been resolved to the default init alias for fields without an explicit alias.
Attribute exposes alias_is_default to distinguish auto-generated aliases from explicit aliases, even when both aliases have the same text value.

If Attribute.evolve() changes name without receiving a new alias, the alias is recomputed from the new name only when the previous alias was auto-generated; otherwise the existing explicit alias is retained.
If Attribute.evolve() receives an explicit alias update, the resulting attribute records that alias as non-default.
Attribute objects restored from older serialized state infer alias_is_default so pre-upgrade serialized metadata remains usable.
acceptance_criteria: When a class uses field_transformer and includes a field without an explicit alias, the transformer should receive that field with the same resolved alias that the finalized class exposes for initialization.
When a field has an explicit alias, alias_is_default should report false even if that explicit alias matches attrs' default derived alias for the field name.
When Attribute.evolve(name=...) is called without alias on an attribute whose alias was auto-generated, the evolved attribute should expose the default alias for the new name.
When Attribute.evolve(name=...) is called without alias on an attribute whose alias was explicitly set, the evolved attribute should keep the explicit alias unchanged.
When field_transformer adds a new Attribute without an alias, the finalized class should expose a usable default alias for that field.
When loading an Attribute object serialized before this upgrade, alias-related behavior should remain consistent with newly created Attribute instances.

task_4.title: Allow NO_OP on_setattr in frozen attrs classes
task_4.description: The upgrade removes an incorrect runtime restriction in attrs so frozen classes can declare field-level `on_setattr=attrs.setters.NO_OP` without failing class creation. This aligns `NO_OP` with its intended no-hook semantics while preserving the existing prohibition on real `on_setattr` hooks for frozen classes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that frozen attrs classes accept field-level `on_setattr=attrs.setters.NO_OP` as a valid no-op configuration instead of rejecting the class definition, while continuing to reject frozen classes that use actual `on_setattr` hooks.

expectation.grounded: When defining a frozen class with `attr.s(frozen=True)` or equivalent frozen attrs behavior, `attr.ib(on_setattr=attrs.setters.NO_OP)` must be accepted the same way as `on_setattr=None`. Frozen classes must still raise `ValueError` when a field configures any non-no-op `on_setattr` hook.
expectation.conceptual: Frozen attrs models should allow an explicit no-op `on_setattr` setting because it does not change frozen behavior. Only configurations that introduce real setattr processing should remain invalid for frozen classes.

constraints.grounded: Do not change frozen-class enforcement for active `on_setattr` hooks other than `attrs.setters.NO_OP`. Preserve the observable distinction that `None` and `attrs.setters.NO_OP` are both allowed on frozen fields, but other hooks are rejected during class definition.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the fix narrowly scoped to explicit no-op setattr handling. The upgrade must not weaken the immutability contract of frozen classes or broaden support for actual setattr hooks.

behavior: A frozen attrs class may define a field with `on_setattr=attrs.setters.NO_OP` without failing class creation.
`attrs.setters.NO_OP` is treated as equivalent to having no `on_setattr` hook for frozen-class validation.
Frozen attrs classes continue to reject non-no-op `on_setattr` hooks with `ValueError`.
acceptance_criteria: When a user defines a frozen attrs class and a field sets `on_setattr=attrs.setters.NO_OP`, the class should be created successfully.
When a user defines a frozen attrs class and a field sets `on_setattr=None`, the behavior should remain accepted and unchanged.
When a user defines a frozen attrs class and a field sets a real `on_setattr` hook such as a validator hook, class creation should still fail with `ValueError`.

task_5.title: Allow attrs.fields() to accept attrs instances
task_5.description: The update expands attrs.fields() so callers can pass an attrs-decorated instance as well as an attrs class. Instance inputs should resolve to the same field metadata exposed by the instance's class, while unsupported objects must still fail with TypeError and existing class-based behavior must remain unchanged.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that attrs.fields() accepts attrs instances in addition to attrs classes, returning the instance type's field metadata while continuing to reject unsupported inputs.

expectation.grounded: attrs.fields() must accept either an attrs class or an instance of an attrs class. When given an attrs instance, it should return the same field metadata tuple exposed for type(instance). When given an object that is neither a class nor an instance of an attrs class, it should raise TypeError. Existing support for valid class inputs, including generic classes, must remain intact.
expectation.conceptual: Consumers should be able to introspect field definitions through attrs.fields() using either the class itself or an instance created from that class. Unsupported objects should still fail with a type error, and previously supported class-based usage should behave the same.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the field metadata returned for existing valid class inputs. Instance support is limited to actual attrs instances; arbitrary instances must not be treated as valid. Rejection of unsupported inputs must remain a TypeError.
constraints.conceptual: The new convenience behavior should not alter results for existing callers or broaden acceptance beyond real attrs objects. Invalid inputs should continue to fail clearly instead of being silently accepted.

behavior: attrs.fields() accepts an instance of an attrs-decorated class as input.
For an attrs instance, attrs.fields(instance) returns the field metadata for the instance's class, matching the result of attrs.fields(type(instance)).
Passing a non-attrs instance to attrs.fields() raises TypeError.
Calling attrs.fields() with supported class inputs, including previously supported generic classes, continues to work as before.
acceptance_criteria: When attrs.fields() is called with an attrs class, it should return that class's field metadata exactly as before.
When attrs.fields() is called with an instance of an attrs class, it should return the same field metadata exposed for the instance's class.
When attrs.fields() is called with an instance that is not an attrs instance, it should raise TypeError.
When attrs.fields() is called with other previously supported class forms, including supported generic classes, their behavior should remain unchanged.
